extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 42ndIntemational Conference on Machine Leaming
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors used SEART GitHub search to filter repositories, extracted task instances using SWE-Bench's script, and semi-automatically collected versions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world software engineering tasks sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dependencies were manually configured for each task instance, and an execution-based validation script was used to ensure the gold patch passed more unit tests than the original code, filtering out failed instances.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity, but could also impact jobs and be misused to create malicious code.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a long-tail distribution of tasks across repositories, and training on all successful trajectories introduces a bias toward easier tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The environment is limited by its diversity in terms of the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training language model based software engineering agents and verifiers.
